name: cool_all_day_heat_all_day
description: Cold day with high of 58F — indoor starts at 68F, below comfort_heat=70F. Cold classification sets heat mode. Heat applies at comfort_heat=70F. No nat vent window (outdoor too cold). Bedtime setback applies at night.
notes: Issue #1537 (owner-approved golden change; re-derived 2026-11-13, owner approved: harness thermostats report hvac_action (#1537)): the thermostat now reports heating from 06:01 (68 F is past its own 68.5 F start point under the 70 F setpoint) and, with the scripted room never reaching its 71.5 F stop point, is still heating at 22:00. Production's settling guard reads the reported run (comfort-edge-selection-spec R3: 'heating ran 0 min ago') and holds the bedtime heat->cool margin switch (comfort_switch_held, zone margin), so bedtime now sends heat at the 64 F setback (set_temperature heat 64) instead of set_hvac_mode cool + cool 72 F. That held heat comes from the harness thermostat's 1.5 F stop swing (the scripted room never reaches 71.5 F, so the furnace never stops), not from the physics of a real thermostat: with a realistic 0.5 F swing the furnace stops at 70.5 F and production arms cool 72 F at bedtime as before, a pre-existing production issue tracked as #1541 (open). This golden records the current behaviour under the harness swing and cites #1541; it is not evidence that the bedtime cool arming is fixed. Assertions unchanged. (a) Effectiveness: the assertions still fail without the classification or the bedtime setback; they do not discriminate the hold (setback_applied 64 F was recorded either way). (b) Docs<->production: comfort-edge-selection-spec R3/R2 and sim-harness-spec match production. (c) Occupant: under this harness the AC is not armed at bedtime while the furnace still runs; on a real thermostat with a tight swing the occupant can still get cool 72 F armed on a cold night (#1541).
Covers the standard cold day pattern: heat on all day, no nat vent, setback at night.
Outdoor never reaches indoor levels — no nat vent activation is possible.

Bedtime setback uses DEFAULT_SLEEP_HEAT (64F, a flat default reformatted to a real tuned installation's own value in the architecture-reset session) since no thermal model or explicit sleep_heat is configured.
This is a gap-filling scenario: confirms heat mode is applied and maintained, setback fires correctly.

events.note: Cold winter morning: indoor 68F (below comfort_heat=70F), outdoor 38F.
Mid-morning: heat has brought indoor to 70.5F. Outdoor still 42F — no nat vent.

Afternoon: outdoor reached 56F (peak for the day). Still below indoor 70F — nat vent activation guard: outdoor < indoor but indoor exactly at comfort_heat=70F (not above), so nat vent will not activate if door opens.
Bedtime: heat setback fires. DEFAULT_SLEEP_HEAT=64F (no explicit sleep_heat configured). Floor is setback_heat=62F so 64F is above floor.

assertions.reason: No new event at 9 AM that changes state — last decision was classification_applied at 6:01 AM. Temp update with nat vent inactive and no sensors open produces no new decision.
Bedtime setback: heat mode, DEFAULT_SLEEP_HEAT=64F (no explicit sleep_heat configured). Above setback_heat=62F floor.

verdict.summary: Cold day applies heat at comfort target all day; bedtime setback fires at DEFAULT_SLEEP_HEAT
verdict.observed_behavior: classification_applied (heat, 70F) at 6 AM → setback_applied (64F) at bedtime, heat kept (the bedtime switch to cool is held while the harness furnace still runs; with a realistic 0.5 F swing production arms cool 72 F, open issue #1541). Re-derived 2026-11-13, owner approved: harness thermostats report hvac_action (#1537)
verdict.expected_behavior: Continuous heat mode all day; no nat vent (outdoor too cold); bedtime setback to 64F
